codex_consultation.block_reason: pretool-bash-safety.sh blocks ANY bash invocation containing the substring `happy-restart` (per concern C3 — only the user from a real TTY may operate on this script). Codex CLI is a bash invocation, so the prompt body's mention of the script name triggers the block. This was BA-predicted (codex_consult.status=failed_hook_blocked in context JSON).
codex_consultation.circumvention_rejection_rationale: Subagent Hook Discipline rule 1: when a hook rejects a command, PAUSE and report — do NOT circumvent via shell wrappers, intermediary scripts, hook-source recon, or hook-file edits. Substring obfuscation (e.g., concatenation tricks) would be a circumvention.
self_review_questions_covered: Q1: cross-fs mv weakens atomicity? — likelihood low (single NVMe sda1); mitigation noted as belt-and-suspenders only
Q2: awk range expression portability (gawk/mawk/busybox)? — POSIX-compatible; trivial mitigation (existing wc -l ≥ 400 catches any divergence)
Q3: sed $d portability (BSD vs GNU)? — Ubuntu ships GNU sed; identical behavior; no mitigation needed
Q4: encoding edge cases (BOM, NEL, U+2028)? — markdown is plain ASCII; head -1 shebang gate catches stray bytes at body start
Q5: SIGPIPE from head/tail in streaming pipe? — N/A (head/tail are run on the staged tempfile AFTER the pipe completes, not in the streaming pipe)
Q6: shell quoting interactions with markdown body content? — N/A (cat reads bytes; awk/sed get bytes through pipe; no shell expansion of body content)
Q7: mktemp permission / /tmp full? — short-circuits via && before destination is touched
Q8: destination is symlink? — orchestrator-asserted regular file; recovery via .bak.preapply works in either case
Q9: ext4 durability after mv? — kernel journal handles rename; very low likelihood
Q10: race with concurrent invocation? — out of scope (single user, single TTY)
Q11: chmod +x vs explicit 755? — minor; +x is sufficient given mv from mktemp default 600 → 711
